transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I suppose I'm just here because... I've been getting stuck on a few things lately. Little routines, I guess you could call them. Um, like washing my hands again after I adjust my wrist brace. Or... checking the stove, checking the front door. Sometimes I just sort of... count through the steps in my head before I leave the house. It's just... it's making me late for things. Even when I know I've already done them.
Do you have any thoughts that keep repeating in your mind and are difficult to control?

I suppose... yes. Sometimes when I'm just sitting at home reading, or getting ready for my shift at the museum... an ugly little thought just keeps barging in. 

Usually it's that I've left something unsafe, or... touched something unclean. It's unpleasant. The idea that I might have somehow put someone at risk just repeats, even though... well, I know perfectly well it's out of proportion.
Do you do these routines, like washing your hands or checking the stove, in response to those unpleasant thoughts?

Yes... I suppose they are. Like I mentioned earlier, I just get stuck doing them. The washing after I touch my brace, rechecking the stove and the door... counting through the steps in my head. 

If I have one of those thoughts, doing the routine is just... what I do to move past it. Even though I know perfectly well I've already done enough. It just ends up making me late.
When you do these routines, are you trying to prevent something bad from happening?

I suppose... yes. It's like I said, I just get stuck doing those little routines. The hand washing after I touch the brace, checking the stove, the door... the counting. 

I just... I do them so nothing bad happens, I guess. Even though I know I've done them already. It just makes me late.
Are you trying to prevent something specific from happening when you do these routines, like someone getting hurt or something bad occurring?

I'm not... I don't really know if it's anything specific. It's mostly just what I said a moment ago. I just get stuck doing these little routines. 

Washing my hands again after I handle my wrist brace, rechecking the stove and the front door... silently counting through the steps before I can leave the house. I do it because... well, I just get stuck. Even when I know perfectly well I've already done enough, I can't seem to stop. And it's starting to make me late for things. I'd... rather not overthink the rest of it, honestly.
Are your repetitive behaviors, such as hand washing or checking, focused on preventing something bad from happening to yourself or to others?

I... I really don't think it's about anything specific like that. I'm not picturing someone getting hurt. It's just... like I keep saying, I just get stuck in these routines. 

The hand washing, the checking the stove and the door, the counting... I just do them. I know I've done enough, but I still do it, and it makes me late. That's... that's really all it is. I don't know why we keep going over this part.
Do you feel less anxious after completing one of these routines?

I'm not really sure. I haven't paid much attention to how I feel afterward. 

I suppose I just... finish the steps, and then I can finally leave the house. I wouldn't necessarily say I feel less anxious, or much of anything, really. It's just... done.
Do you think doing these routines helps you feel less anxious or uncomfortable in any way?

I... I don't know. I really couldn't say. 

Like I said, I just... finish what I'm doing. I haven't really thought about whether it makes me feel better or worse. It's just something I have to get through so I can move on. I don't really want to keep dissecting it.
Do you think that if you didn't do these routines, you would feel more anxious?

I... I suppose I might. I don't know. 

If I don't finish them, I just... I can't leave. I'm stuck until it's done. So maybe I'd feel anxious if I tried to just walk out the door without doing it, but... I don't try that. I just do the routine.
Do you think your repetitive behaviors are attempts to reduce your anxiety?

I... I suppose so. I mean, that's what brings me in, really. I've just gotten stuck doing these... little routines. 

Washing my hands again after I handle my wrist brace, rechecking the stove, making sure the front door is locked... silently counting through the steps before I can leave. I just... I know I've already done enough, but I still do it. And it's starting to make me late for things. So... maybe it is about the anxiety. I don't know.
Is there something specific that you are afraid might happen if you don't complete one of these routines?

I... well. It's just... these thoughts. They just sort of barge in. 

Like if I'm reading at home, or getting ready for my shift at the museum... I'll just get this... ugly little thought that I've left something unsafe. Or that I've touched something unclean. Maybe... somehow put someone at risk. I know perfectly well it's out of proportion, but... I suppose that's what it is.
Is there a specific bad outcome that you fear might happen if you don't complete one of these routines?

I... no, not really. It's not a specific event I'm picturing. Just... that general feeling that something isn't right. That I need to fix it. I don't really think about what would happen if I didn't. I just... know I have to do it.
Do you feel like you need to perform these routines in a specific or perfect way?
I wouldn't say perfect, no. I just... do it until it feels settled. There isn't really a special way it has to be done, if that's what you mean.
Do you feel like you need to perform these routines in a specific order?
No... I don't think so. There isn't a sequence or anything like that. I just... do what I need to do at the time.
Do you experience any disturbing images or thoughts that come into your mind when you're doing these routines?

I... suppose so. I could just be reading at home, or getting ready for my shift at the museum, and... well, this ugly little thought just keeps barging in. Just an idea that I've left something unsafe, or... touched something unclean. Or that I've somehow put someone at risk. I know perfectly well it's out of proportion, but... yes. It happens.
Do you feel like you need to perform these routines until things feel 'just right' or symmetrical in some way?

Not symmetrical, no. I don't... pay attention to anything like that. Like I mentioned, it's just about checking until the worry settles down. It has nothing to do with making things look a certain way.
Do you feel like you need to perform these routines until things feel 'just right'?

I... thought I just answered that. But, no. It isn't about getting some sort of 'just right' feeling. Like I said, it's really only about doing it until the worry settles down. I don't know how else to explain it.
Do you feel like you need to perform these routines in a way that makes you feel like everything is balanced or even?
I... I feel like we're going in circles here. No. It's not about balance. I just... I check things to make the worry stop. That's all it is.
Do you feel like you need to perform these routines in a way that makes you feel like everything is exact?
No. I... I really don't understand why we keep going over the same thing. It isn't about being exact. It's just what I said before.
Do you feel like you need to perform these routines in a way that makes you feel like everything is exact?
I... didn't you just ask me that? I don't know what else to tell you. The answer is still no.
